**Typhoon No. 15 (Chan-hom) is the dominant driver suppressing Tokyo’s peak temperature on August 12, 2026.** Its unusual east-to-west track across Honshu is delivering widespread cloud cover, heavy showers, and advection of cooler marine air over the Kanto region, limiting solar heating and promoting evaporative cooling. Modest upside risk for 28°C remains if rainfall timing or steering shifts allow brief clearing, while historical analogs of typhoon-influenced August days support the market’s downward tilt. New JMA updates on storm position and rainfall timing will be the next key catalysts for any repricing.

This market will resolve based on the highest temperature recorded in the 'Daily Observations' table on Weather Underground, not the figure displayed in the 'Day High & Low' summary section; in the event of any discrepancy between the two, the Daily Observations table shall be the primary resolution source not the Day High & Low section.

This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded at the Wuhan Tianhe International Airport Station in degrees Celsius on 13 Aug '26.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the gear icon next to the search bar and switch the Temperature setting between °F and °C.

This market can not resolve until the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description: Recent forecasts from sources including the Met Office and BBC Weather point to thundershowers and overcast skies over Wuhan on August 13, capping daytime highs near 28°C and aligning with the market's tight clustering around 27–29°C outcomes. Persistent cloud cover reduces incoming solar radiation, while evaporative cooling from scattered rain and high humidity—typical of the Yangtze Valley monsoon pattern—further limits surface heating compared with clear-sky August averages of 32–35°C. Model consensus shows modest variability in precipitation timing and intensity, which could nudge the peak by 1–2°C depending on whether storms arrive before or after peak insolation. Updated runs from global and regional models over the next 48 hours represent the key catalyst likely to refine these probabilities ahead of resolution.
